title: Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (IV: MPMD, Will Tennyson, Alan Thrall.
summary: Fourth episode of NH's channel-grading series, scoring six fitness YouTubers out of 200 on criteria like programming, experience, integrity, black pill, supplements and physique. Scores: Alec Enkiri 141.5, Will Tennyson 127.5, Revival Fitness 132, MorePlatesMoreDates 105.5, Alan Thrall 151, Natural Gallant Bodybuilding 142. Along the way he gives his views on supplements, TRT, clickbait, content recycling and what makes good fitness advice.
claims: The grading system scores each channel out of 200 across criteria including programming, experience, integrity, usefulness, character, dogmatism, originality, black pill, humor, parasocial, empathy, god complex, production, science, clickbait, recycling, conciseness, seniority, supplements and physique
Alec Enkiri gets 10 for integrity because he was the first to call out Athlean-X as a fraud while a small channel and never backed down; Athlean-X was later caught using fake weights
Taking advice from an athlete like Enkiri will not serve pure hypertrophy goals well
Enkiri disproved the claim that athleticism cannot be trained by raising his own and clients' vertical jump and 40-yard dash
The best stance on supplements is to never mention them; Enkiri also fought the turkesterone craze
Fitness channels that only post information die; you have to balance info with some clickbait or drama
Former fat people who got lean and muscular, like Will Tennyson, are rare and valuable role models for obese young men
Associating with scammy supplement sellers lowers your integrity even if you don't scam yourself
Edutainment tends to drift until the entertainment fully replaces the education
Supplement promotion is more harmful the larger and younger the audience
Promoting blood tests and testosterone products that funnel young men to TRT clinics is a sell-out; TRT is the worst kind of supplement
Not all bulks are equal; a clean bulk differs from just eating everything, and calling it all the same lacks nuance
Advice built on pick-up artist ideas and that women only want the top 20% of men spreads the black pill to young men
Experience-based channels tend to be the best; NH's science grade rewards experience or correct use of the scientific process
Enhanced lifters' hypertrophy advice like how to grow big shoulders simply doesn't work for naturals
Anyone selling testosterone boosters is a scam artist
PED-focused content that is 28 minutes of danger and 2 minutes of 'it makes you bigger' still pushes teenagers onto drugs because they only retain the gains part
Alan Thrall popularized following a written program instead of doing random workouts in the gym
Alan Thrall actually ran every program he reviewed, which is more valuable than judging programs on paper
Handling a diet controversy by saying 'I eat eggs and get my bloodwork' is better than trading cherry-picked studies
Promote real whole food rather than supplements
Natural Gallant Bodybuilding focuses almost entirely on programming, which is the most important thing for natural bodybuilders
Finding the range of motion that works best for you is not dogmatism; it is not the same as preaching only short ROM
Genetics exist but should never be an excuse; play the hand you were dealt
Take advice from lifters with average structures who still built great physiques rather than people born with a Greek-god frame
When you only talk programming you run out of things to say by video 600 or 700
Lifters with long experience but no published papers are still a library of valid information
